children: may have to alter its future flight plans if fuel prices stay elevated, Chief Executive Robert Isom said on Wednesday, as the carrier relies on stronger fares and demand to offset higher expenses.

Speaking at a Morgan Stanley conference, Isom said the airline was confident in its forecast for third-quarter revenue growth of 16% to 19%. He also said he expected most of the recent improvement in revenue to persist.

expects higher fuel prices to add about $1 billion to its costs in the fourth quarter, according to Chief Financial Officer Devon May. Each additional penny in fuel costs translates into roughly $10 million in expenses for the airline.

also expects to adjust its operations if fuel prices remain high. Chief Financial Officer Mike Leskinen said the carrier could make changes extending into the first quarter and beyond in 2027, adding that some December flights would not operate.
had already reduced scheduled flights by 5% in the second and third quarters, targeting weaker off-peak routes and reducing service at Chicago O'Hare.
has benefited from higher fares and premium products, including increased revenue from the front of its aircraft, helping offset part of the fuel cost increase.

title: American Airlines flags potential capacity changes as fuel costs rise
